work_completed: The first acceptance run had 78 passing and 1 failing: `test_r5_an_item_naming_a_test_that_matches_no_case_fails_its_line`. When the README named a test that matched no collected case, the runner added a made-up count of 1 to that line's `failed`. The line was correctly marked fail, but its counts no longer matched the tests that ran. KPI success-1 says each line reports "the counts of tests passed and failed under each line", and design note §4 already treats a line with no matching case as fail with zero counts. So I changed the code to the specification: such a line is still marked `fail`, unnamed, and its counts are only the counts of tests that ran (`src/gov/accept/runner.py`, `_report`). I wrote the unit test change first and saw it fail before the fix. After the fix the second acceptance run passed in full, and `gov accept` passes on this ticket.

risks: A line that fails because a named test is missing now shows `failed: 0` next to `outcome: fail`, so the counts alone don't explain the failure. This is the same as the existing rule that a line with no matching case fails with zero counts, and naming the missing test is forbidden.
lessons: In this ticket's output, a line's `passed`, `failed` and `skipped` are always counts of tests that actually ran. Anything that makes a line fail without a test failing changes only the line's `outcome`, never its counts.
